core_obligations: Left exactness (proof line 1801): the inclusion of sheaves into presheaves preserves kernels, so it is left exact and its right derived functors exist.
Describe the derived functors (proof lines 1802-1805): choose an injective resolution F -> I^bullet in Mod(O); then R^p i(F) is by definition the p-th cohomology presheaf of the complex I^bullet.
Identify the sections (proof lines 1806-1812): over an object U of C the sections of R^p i(F) are ker(I^p(U) -> I^{p+1}(U)) / im(I^{p-1}(U) -> I^p(U)), which is exactly the definition of H^p(U, F).
proof_roadmap: Note that the inclusion functor is left exact.
Compute its right derived functors from an injective resolution.
The resulting presheaf has, over U, kernel modulo image of the section complex.
That is the definition of the cohomology group H^p(U, F), giving the stated description of R^p i.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the right derived functors of the inclusion of sheaves into presheaves: they form the cohomology presheaf U -> H^p(U, F) (statement lines 1786-1798). The proof is a definitional computation: left exactness of the forgetful functor is immediate, and after choosing an injective resolution in Mod(O) the derived functors are the cohomology presheaves of the resolution complex, whose sections over U are kernel modulo image of the section complex, which is the definition of H^p(U, F) (proof lines 1801-1812). The content is the identification of a presheaf of sections with a cohomology group, with no further construction. The claim is H2: one definition unfolded carefully.
